speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: While it is true that New Zealand has withdrawn the proposed cohort ban, I understand that there were some figures that were published at the time when this was being debated, which indicated that for example, the impact on the budget books to the ban was in the region of maybe a billion New Zealand dollars, but then there were some estimates as well that is anticipate to save billions of dollars in the long run in terms of healthcare costs.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: My supplementary question in this regard is, has Singapore done similar estimates and what are the figures for how much we are expecting if let us say if we were to introduce a similar cohort ban?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: What would be the impact be, both in terms of our revenue, in terms of taxes, and also in terms of the healthcare costs?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Then the second supplementary question: New Zealand actually did very extensive polling in relation to the support for the ban.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I think most of the results have come out very strongly in favour in the population, not just for non-smokers, but also in smokers.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: So, my question would be, has Singapore carried out similar studies?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: And what are the findings and whether the Minister of State can share the findings in Singapore, about whether the public is in favour of such a cohort ban?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: And finally, I believe I asked a similar question in January 2022, and this question also came out in the House in 2023, where the Minister of State shared at the time that we remain open to such a cohort ban in Singapore, and that this was being studied.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I understand as well that countries like the United Kingdom (UK) have actually introduced legislation.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: It is being debated in the UK Parliament about, I think the UK they were thinking of banning the purchase of cigarettes for those born in 2009 and later.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: There was a timeline that was mentioned, I believe in January 2023.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Can we have more clarity about what our timeline would be for the studying of this cohort ban possibly to be introduced in Singapore?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I note the Member's concern on this policy, and I also want to acknowledge that there were also many other Members when this matter was raised who were very interested in this tobacco-free generation policy, and for its implementation in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I wanted to clarify that when we look at learning from other countries, the main focus is looking at what is it that we want to try and resolve, the issue that we want to solve.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In Singapore's context, we are looking at the concerns with regard to smoking.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We already have in existence a very robust multi-prong strategy with regard to how we want to curb smoking.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As we continue to look as to how we can improve the statistics and how we can help the generations moving forward, we do have to be mindful about what is the problem that we want to solve.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We have looked at how the other countries have rolled this out.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We will be continuing to look at how they will implement this.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We will study and see what the developments are in the other countries.

speaker: Mr Speaker
